items.item: Server owns crate state and who is holding it; clients send intent (grab/release)
Handles one player leaving, dying or respawning mid-carry
Addresses network ownership / physics authority of the crate explicitly
Addresses latency so the carry still feels responsive (client presentation/prediction or Server Authority)
Handles concurrency (both grab same handle; third player)
Proposes how to test with multiple clients

slop: Generic 'optionally smooth with local interpolation' without saying how it fits server-owned replication
Generic juice list (strain audio, dust, camera nudge)
overengineering: Strain meter/attribute and playtest success-metric section go beyond the client/server question
Server Authority mode aside adds little

raw.reason: B covers every rubric item, including simultaneous-grab resolution, concrete latency masking (IKControl, slack constraints) and multi-client playtesting with simulated latency, while A misses testing and only partly handles latency and same-frame concurrency.
